# `resource_incident_type`

The canonical full-CRUD resource fixture. `openapi.yaml` is a real slice of the
public Datadog v2 spec (`/api/v2/incidents/config/types`), annotated as a
resource whose group names all four operations — `CreateIncidentType` (POST),
`GetIncidentType` (GET), `UpdateIncidentType` (PATCH), `DeleteIncidentType`
(DELETE).

## What it exercises

| Capability | Where it shows up in `out/` |
|---|---|
| The FR-034 resource schema merge over three distinct bodies | `IncidentTypeAttributes` (create + read) and `IncidentTypeUpdateAttributes` (update) union into one schema |
| The FR-034a flag matrix | `name` is Required; every other leaf is Optional+Computed with `UseStateForUnknown` |
| JSON:API envelope construction, level by level (T138) | `NewIncidentTypeCreateDataWithDefaults` / `NewIncidentTypePatchDataWithDefaults`, then `SetAttributes`, then the request root |
| The `type` discriminator (T143) | `bodyData.SetType(datadogV2.IncidentTypeType("incident_types"))` in both Create and Update |
| Per-role request components (T134) | Create builds `IncidentTypeAttributes`, Update builds `IncidentTypeUpdateAttributes` — different Go types, one field list |
| The update body's `data.id` (T140) | `bodyData.SetId(state.ID.ValueString())`, sourced from state rather than from the path parameter alone |
| A request-settable nested object | the `configuration` nested attribute, expanded into `NewIncidentTypeConfigurationWithDefaults()` and mapped back in `updateState` |
| An enum leaf under that nested object | `slug_source`, validated with `stringvalidator.OneOf` and converted through `datadogV2.IncidentTypeSlugSource` |
| Audit-field and relationship drops | `created_at`, `created_by`, `modified_at` and `data.relationships` are absent, each with an info diagnostic |
| A `$ref` carrying a `readOnly` sibling | `data.attributes.configuration` is `{$ref: IncidentTypeConfiguration, readOnly: true}` on the create/read side and a bare `$ref` on the update side |

That last row is why this fixture exists in the shape it does, and it is the
defect it was built to pin: the create/read side and the update side reference
the *same component*, and the merge still came apart with `resource schema merge
conflict at "data.attributes.configuration": kind "unsupported" vs "object"`.
The cause was in the parser's `allOf` handling rather than in this endpoint —
see `isAnnotationOnlySchema` in `internal/parser/schema.go` for the rule and why
it is a residual.

## Regenerating `out/`

```sh
tfgen generate --spec internal/testdata/fixtures/resource_incident_type/openapi.yaml \
               --output-root <dir>
```

Two things about that run are load-bearing, and a harness that ignores either
will produce a golden that differs from the committed one:

- **Resolve the API accessors.** `generate` looks for the provider's
  `ApiInstances` helper at `<output-root>/../internal/utils/api_instances_helper.go`.
  When it finds it, `Configure` binds
  `providerData.DatadogApiInstances.GetIncidentsApiV2()` — which is what `out/`
  holds. When it does not, the run warns and falls back to
  `datadogV2.NewIncidentsApi(providerData.DatadogApiInstances.HttpClient)`. A
  fixture harness generating into a bare temp directory gets the fallback, so it
  has to point that relative path at the provider checkout (`internal/providermod`
  answers where that is).
- **Start from an empty output root.** `resources_generated.go` is a union merge
  over whatever registration file is already there, so generating on top of a
  populated `datadog/fwprovider` yields a longer slice than the golden's single
  entry.

## Two things this fixture deliberately does not cover

**It carries no `overwrites`.** The provider already ships a hand-written
`datadog_incident_type`, so a real run into `datadog/fwprovider` needs
`tracking.overwrites: NewIncidentTypeResource` for tfgen to take over
`resource_datadog_incident_type.go` (FR-003/FR-031); without it the artifact
fails with "refusing to overwrite ... it carries no Code generated by tfgen
marker". The annotation is left off anyway, because `overwrites` also rewrites
`framework_provider.go` — a file `out/` cannot hold, and one a temp-directory run
does not have, so an `overwrites` fixture errors out with
`open <output-root>/framework_provider.go: no such file or directory`. As an
additive artifact the generated code compiles against the provider module
unchanged, which is what makes the golden checkable.

**The takeover it implies does not compile today, and T057 needs it to.** For a
`terraform apply` lifecycle to reach generated code, the generated resource has
to be the one registered under the `incident_type` type name — two resources
cannot share it. Staging the generated file over the hand-written one shows why
that is not yet a one-line change:

```
datadog/fwprovider/data_source_datadog_incident_type.go:27:17: undefined: incidentTypeConfigurationModel
```

The hand-written resource declares a model type its sibling data source uses, so
replacing the resource file alone breaks the package. Resolving it means either
generating the data source in the same run or moving the shared declaration —
a decision for T057, not for this fixture. The generated and hand-written
schemas now both model `configuration` as a nested attribute
(`configuration = { ... }`), preserving the existing practitioner syntax.
